Subject: Reserved capacity: surge buffer + price-escrow proposal for NimbusAI

James / Priya —

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Per our discussion, attached is a refined reserved capacity proposal that folds in: a modest surge buffer (10% burst pool), a price-escrow clause tied to a monthly GPU index, and a one-time onboarding credit. Key asks from Nimbus were predictable monthly spend and a mechanism for protection if spot GPU prices spike.

High level (see attached redwood_reserved_proposal_v3.pdf):
- Committed baseline: 1200 AUR hours / month (Aurora instances)
- Surge buffer: +120 hours / month (10%), billed only when used; separate bucket at discounted committed rate
- Price-escrow: tiered adjustment if normalized monthly GPU cost exceeds baseline by >15% (triggers partial credit or blended pass-through)
- One-time setup credit: $25k for migration and fine-tuning

Please review the proposal and the fleet_pricing_model.xlsx (sensitivity tabs included). If Nimbus is comfortable, we can tee up a short executive approval for a 24-month commit with a 9-month ramp.

Next steps I propose:
1) You flag anything material in the pricing model by EOD Thursday.
2) If acceptable, we route the proposal to finance for a formal discount approval and get an exec pre-approval on the price-escrow language.
3) Sign and DocuSign link.

– Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick notes after a skim of the model:
- The surge buffer looks reasonable, but Priya and I want clarity on how burst billing appears on the invoice (line item vs. blended).
- The price-escrow mechanism is interesting; we need a cap on our liability and a clear runbook for when the trigger occurs (notification window, lookback period).
- Can we get an option for a 12-month initial commit with an automatic extension if usage stays within +/-10%? The 24-month is fine but our CFO prefers shorter initial terms.

I'll ask our finance lead to review the fleet_pricing_model.xlsx. Can you loop in your finance/ops contact for an ops-runbook and invoice example?

Karthik / David —

Looping finance and product ops. I reviewed the pricing model; we can accept the surge buffer as a separate invoice line (recommended) and the price-escrow clause needs a tighter trigger. Proposed internal changes:
- Trigger: 20% deviation sustained over two consecutive monthly normalized GPU cost observations (rather than one month)
- Cap: Customer liability capped at 30% of the monthly committed spend in any billing month where trigger fires
- Runbook: 14-day notification window + 30-day remediation period before applying credits/blended adjustments

If Nimbus wants an initial 12-month term, we'll need a small uplift (3.5%) on the committed unit price to offset shorter tenor risk. That said, we can offer an executive concession to reduce the uplift by 1.5% if they agree to a 15-month auto-extension clause.

Attaching exec_approval_note.txt to capture the ask for approval.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Finance | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

James / Priya —

Thanks for the quick reply and useful feedback. A few clarifications and an updated offer inline:
- Invoicing: Surge buffer will appear as a separate line item with per-hour usage at the committed unit rate; monthly summaries will show burst hours consumed.
- Escrow trigger/update: We can move to Marissa's recommended trigger (20% sustained over two months) with the 30% cap on monthly liability.
- Term: We can offer a 12-month initial term at a +3.5% uplift, or a 15-month auto-extension at +2.0% uplift (executive concession).

To expedite, if Nimbus is comfortable with the 15-month auto-extension path we'll route for expedited exec signoff and prepare a DocuSign. If you prefer 12-month, let me know and I'll flag for standard finance approval (slower).

Can you confirm preference today so we can circulate the final for signatures tomorrow?

Best,
Karthik
